description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
1 layer 1 head: one-hot pos/token embeddings; query pos q attends to fixed source position (reversed word order, separators from '_' slots) and copies token to output logits.
Like PosCopy1L but attention writes copied token (x3) into the token dims, d_model=T+V, no separate output slot.

noOutSlot, C=1, value gain 2 instead of 3 (still must beat own-token residual).
noOutSlot, C=1, value gain 1 (I expected a tie with the own-token residual to hurt; it did not, because LayerNorm rescales the attention output).
noOutSlot, C=0.75, value gain 1.
Clean version: queries only defined for the 11 answer-producing positions (q=11..21), C=3, value gain 1, d_model=T+V, 1 layer 1 head.

Clean version (queries only for answer positions q=11..21, C=3, value gain 1, d_model=T+V, 1 layer 1 head), max_seq_len=22 (seq_len-1), d_ff=0 (MLP removed).

1 layer 1 head, d_ff=0. Separate key-id dims (prompt pos 0..10) and pointer dims (answer step j at pos 11+j); W_q maps pointer j -> key id of the source char. C=5, value gain 1, d_model=2*11+V.
Same as PointerKeyCopy1L but C=1.

1 layer 1 head, d_ff=0, d_model=8+V. Prompt positions carry a 4-bit +-1 key code; answer positions carry the 4-bit code of the prompt position they should copy; W_q/W_k identity on the code dims, so attention peaks where codes match. C=1, value gain 1.
d_model=18: position codes 4-bit +-1, token codes 5-bit +-1, separate 5-dim output slot, head decodes by dot product with token codes. C=3: attention too soft.
Same as BinaryCodeAll1L with C=10.
d_model=13: BinaryCodeAll1L without the separate output slot (copied 5-bit token code added onto the own-token code, value gain 10), C=10.
d_model=13 variant, value gain 40, C=10.
d_model=13 variant, value gain 40, C=30.
d_model=13 variant, value gain 40, C=100.
d_model=13 variant, value gain 200, C=100: same 2 errors as gain 40, so the residual errors are not about gain (suspected LayerNorm mean-shift bias favouring token codes with more +1 bits).

1 layer 1 head, d_ff=0, d_model=15, no output slot. Positions: 4-bit +-1 key/pointer codes. Tokens: 7-bit constant-weight (3 of 7 are +1) +-1 codes, so LayerNorm's mean shift is the same for every token logit. Value gain 40, C=100. Fixes the d13 errors.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=10, value gain 40.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=3, value gain 40: attention too soft.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=10, value gain 10.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=10, value gain 3.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=10, value gain 1.

Control for the constant-weight hypothesis: same d15 model, C=10, value gain 40, but tokens use plain 7-bit binary codes (not constant weight). 97.5% vs 100%, consistent with the LayerNorm mean-shift explanation.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=6, value gain 40.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=4.5, value gain 40.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=3.5, value gain 40: attention starts to be too soft.
ConstWeightCode1L_d15 with C=6, value gain 1: 8/200; with low gain and moderate C the own-token residual or blended attention wins.

Final configuration: 1 layer 1 head, d_ff=0, d_model=15; 4-bit +-1 position key/pointer codes, 7-bit constant-weight token codes, C=10, value gain 1 (same weights as ConstWeightCode1L_d15_C10_g1, rerun).
